analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch adds one paragraph at head lines 1561-1569 describing how LocalTokenizerBridge.decode releases trailing <0xHH> byte-fallback tokens so detokenizer segment restarts cannot land inside a multibyte character. The supplied units (head lines 2027-2839) fall outside the changed range, so they are unchanged surrounding documentation. I read them for context: MTP acceptance, sampling, Qwen JSON constraints, tool parsers, MiMo and the vision caps. Nothing in them is modified.

The doc change adds no executable code, no new trust boundary, no new endpoint and no change to key, attestation or cache handling. It touches no threat-model asset directly. The described behavior is local text decoding in the provider, which handles decrypted prompt and output text in memory (A-001, TB-007). It adds no new logging, persistence or network exposure. The cache-related text in the surrounding units (T-041) does not alter the HMAC-keyed names, the TTL or the scoping. I did not see the underlying Swift code (LocalTokenizerLoader.swift), so the claimed decoder behavior is unverified. The next pass should check that code if it is in the PR. The check should confirm that releasing a trailing byte run cannot emit malformed output or affect stop-string holdback, and that the code does not log content. The visible evidence is documentation only, so I raise no finding.
